text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rate on service-discovery SRV lookups in eu-central-1a (euc1a) — multiple clusters reporting 'no SRV records' and gRPC routing failures. Trigger: healthcheck spike > 5% for 12m. Escalation: oncall.
Alex (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Starting triage — grabbing logs from coreDNS/consul and checking recent deploys.

Tilly (sre): I'm seeing repeated failures from the consul-agent on nodes in euc1a: "failed to query SRV: context deadline exceeded" and intermittent raft leader changes. Not global — mostly euc1a.

Raj (netops): Any recent peering/route changes in euc1a? I don't see infra change events in the last 24h. LLDP/peering status normal. I'll check networking plane for packet loss.

Mei (eng-runtime): From the routing side we have a few requests falling back to older model variants because backend SRV resolution returned empty. That explains increase in 5xx from some API customers. Dumping a service discovery trace now.

Alex (oncall): Paste the trace. Also, are coreDNS pods OOMing or restarting?

Tilly (sre): coreDNS pods in kube-system on euc1a show high latencies for SRV responses. cpu usage ~ 85% on 3 pods, one pod RestartCount=2 in last hour. Logs show series of warnings: `read udp xx.xx.xx.xx:53: i/o timeout` and `cache: entry negative TTL exceeded`.

Mei (eng-runtime): Example from request path: `client -> coreDNS(euc1a) -> consul-agent(euc1a) -> consul-server-raft` — consul-server raft leader seems to be flapping between two replicas, causing higher latency. Some consul servers returning 500 on /v1/catalog/service queries.

Raj (netops): I spun a quick pcap between two consul servers, saw sporadic retransmits and ~1.5% packet loss across the AZ fabric for a short window starting 2135677400. That aligns with when the errors started. Might be noisy fabric or a switch with microbursts.

Alex (oncall): Customer impact? Which tenants affected and severity?

Luis (support): Looking at request traces, ~300 unique API keys hit SRV lookup failures in the last hour. Majority are background jobs and retries, but 5 high-traffic customers saw visible increased latency and ~10% error rate for generation calls. I've DM'd their CSMs.

Ana (product): P1 for affected customers who have SLAs. We should prepare an incident banner if this is going to be >1h.

Tilly (sre): Immediate mitigation proposals:
- Move coreDNS pods to healthy nodes in euc1b via `kubectl cordon/drain` alternatives (risk: pod churn)
- Add iptables rule to prefer cross-AZ consul-server endpoints (but that's risky)
- Increase coreDNS replicas in euc1a to absorb load (fast)
- Force a stable consul leader via `consul operator raft list-peers` and demote noisy node (requires care)

Mei (eng-runtime): Quickest safe step is scale coreDNS replicas x2 in euc1a and adjust healthchecks to reduce negative TTL churn. We can also temporarily route service-discovery queries to euc1b if cross-AZ routing is healthy.

Raj (netops): Cross-AZ path euc1a->euc1b shows <0.1% loss currently. If we failover discovery queries to euc1b the added latency is +12ms median but should restore correctness.

Alex (oncall): Do it. Tilly/Mei, please coordinate. I'll ping if any customer escalations.

Tilly (sre): Scaling coreDNS now: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/coredns --replicas=6 --context=cluster-euc1a` -> scaling event started.

deploy-bot: rollout/coredns scaling to 6 replicas initiated by Tilly via CLI — 3/6 pods ready.

Mei (eng-runtime): I'm updating runtime config to prefer consul endpoints in euc1b for SRV queries: toggling feature flag `sd.prefer_remote_zone`=true for euc1a-runtime pool. This will route discovery RPCs to euc1b consul servers. Applying now.

Alex (oncall): Noted. Any expected brief blips?

Mei (eng-runtime): There will be ~15-30s of added latency for in-flight lookups. No service restarts.

Tilly (sre): coreDNS pods stabilized after scaling, CPU dropped to ~40% and negative TTL logs decrease. Consul leader appears stable after routing change — raft leader settled on node c-03 at 2135678500.

Raj (netops): Network fabric telemetry shows packet loss returned to baseline at ~2135678600. Looks like a transient hardware microburst. I flagged fabric team to inspect the switch.

Luis (support): Error rates dropping for customers — most show normalizing within last 7m. The 5 impacted customers now showing <1% errors. Continuing to monitor.

Ana (product): Preparing a customer notification draft. Keep me posted on final RCA points we can share (root cause: AZ fabric microbursts causing consul raft instability -> SRV lookup failures; mitigations: local scaling + cross-AZ routing).

Alex (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 10m for a meeting. Tilly will take over oncall for the next hour. Make sure to capture steps in incident timeline.

Tilly (sre): Taking over. I'll keep the monitoring window open for 2h and coordinate with netops and runtime. Current status: mitigations applied, error rate trending to normal. Next actions: 1) fabric team postmortem ticket, 2) verify consul logs for any state corruption, 3) create runbook updates for SRV negative TTL flaps.

Mei (eng-runtime): Note for follow-up: consider adding automatic cross-zone fallback for consul queries when leader churn detected, and add circuit-breaker on SRV negative cache to avoid high negative TTL refresh.

Raj (netops): Filed ticket NF-2134 with fabric team (assigned to @switchops). Link: https://infra.example.com/tickets/NF-2134.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV2 — majority of customers functioned with degraded performance, small subset impacted with higher error-rate.

Luis (support): We'll hold customer-facing banner until we confirm stability for 30m. CSMs notified.

Tilly (sre): Handoff note for next oncall: timeline, commands used, flags toggled (`sd.prefer_remote_zone=true`), consul leader stable on c-03, coreDNS scaled to 6 replicas. I'll follow up with RCA draft after fabric team provides details.

Alex (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving the channel. :tada:

Tilly (sre): Closing real-time mitigation chat. Will reopen if any regressions.

Mei (eng-runtime): Logged follow-up task: RH-1245 (runtime fallback automation).

Luis (support): Marking incident affected customers list and next contact steps in support tracker.

Raj (netops): Monitoring switch health, will post updated telemetry and schedule on-site maintenance if needed.
